Consistent with the Apadāna genre, the poem commemorates the pious deed of an elder who made a meritorious gift of rice gruel (*yāgu*), recounting the past karmic act and its eventual fruit leading to liberation [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five translations of the text in five languages, and notes connections or cross-references with the *Āḷavaka Sutta* (SN 10.12 and Snp 1.10 / PTS Snp 31) as well as the *Upālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 8) [SuttaCentral].
